back: A statement of the cash a business expects to receive and pay out in future periods, with the expected cash balance at the end of each period.
Net cash flow = total receipts - total payments for the period.
Closing balance = opening balance + net cash flow. It becomes the next period's opening balance.

front: What is not in a forecast
back: Depreciation and profit are not cash flows. Credit sales appear when customers pay, not when the sale is made.
Foresee shortages, arrange finance in time, time big payments, support loan applications and control the business.
Late-paying customers, over-stocking, heavy spending on equipment, seasonal sales with steady costs, falling sales and poor forecasting.
Chase debts, offer discounts, use trade credit, factoring, leasing, sale and leaseback, overdraft, cut costs or sell assets.
Change the assumptions (later customer payments, higher costs) and recalculate to see the effect on the balances (what-if analysis).
It is based on estimates, so check how reliable the sales and payment assumptions are and how long and how big any shortage is.
